title: Ordinary invertibility from native cone detection and constructible finiteness
statement: For a forgetful model V on a finite-type model T, let q:H→M be a native morphism with V(H) isomorphic to V(M). Suppose for every native v:K→H, vanishing of the ordinary underlying composite vq forces V(v)=0. Then the ordinary underlying map of q is invertible. This criterion involves no exceptional functor, adjunction, counit or graded Hom assertion.

proof.text: Complete q to a native distinguished triangle and rotate. Its first arrow v has vq=0; the hypothesis and the realization through the faithful section and closure equivalences make its ordinary map zero. The ordinary distinguished triangle therefore splits, so the underlying q is split mono.

The common-stage isomorphism gives an ordinary isomorphism of H and M via rho and the section and closure equivalences. At every cohomological degree and geometric point the split injection induced by q is between finite-dimensional vector spaces of equal dimension, hence is bijective. Conservativity of constructible stalks and of derived cohomology makes q an ordinary isomorphism. Empty schemes and zero objects are included. No faithfulness of native forgetting is assumed.

lean.statement:
theorem native_ordinary_cone_detection (R : Family l D) (T : Space D)
    (V : ForgetModel D l R T) (H M : W D l T) (q : H ⟶ M)
    (e : Nonempty (V.functor.obj H ≅ V.functor.obj M))
    (hq : ∀ (K : W D l T) (v : K ⟶ H),
      WeilComplex.forget.map (v ≫ q) = 0 → V.functor.map v = 0) :
    IsIso (WeilComplex.forget.map q)
